answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Signed workplace check-in streak with QR scans flips the bet — check-ins scanned at the same desk every morning — and the fable lands on the attacker instead. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that check-ins scanned at the same desk every morning — so privacy survives, and the wander is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. Do the arithmetic for a hundred clones: a hundred proofs, each with its own paperwork, hardware, or history, and the zephyr is a budget no epoch payout can repay.
